A.claim: Synchronous ExtendScript and photoshop.jsx DOM getters have no worker mirror. Each getter is a dependent read over IPC (p50 20 us, p99 100 us), and the only budget compares against the old boa session, not the incumbent.

On iOS, QuickJS is native C running inside the app process. A memory-safety bug in the engine takes down the app, and contain/panic=unwind cannot catch a SIGSEGV. Non-interruptible builtins (a native sort, a huge JSON.parse) also defeat Stop-all <= 260 ms, because a thread cannot be killed.

Peer batches queue in the Replica behind any modal transaction, with no time or size bound. This round also lets RunMode::Long commands run inside txn.modal, so multiplayer edits can stall for minutes and the queue can grow without limit. Figma plugins never block multiplayer.

The props text 'overridable only on the last seven' reads as: overridable is allowed only on the trust and lifecycle set. DEC-COM-interceptable-default-false says the reverse: those seven refuse both flags, and Override is allowed on view, selection, nudge and tool commands.

Net commands get two outcomes. Rule 2 says Never (N6), as does CAP-EC-reach-ai-model for *.model.download. CON-COM-exposure@2 and the error table make Net Excluded -9 {Network} under DEC-COM-no-plugin-network. The plugin-visible code and the reason disagree.

This round's edit to the error table did not add the detail kinds that a cross-document requirement asks for: BrowserUnsupported under -8 and UnsupportedVideo{codec} under -1. Gate C20 fails on any unlisted kind, so the FigCraft web and video paths cannot return them.

Audio slots run on an RT thread in the plugin worker process. The budget covers only process() time, not the cross-process wake and return or any added buffering latency. In-process CLAP/AU hosts add 0 blocks of latency.

Overlay commands are recorded in Actions and listed to MCP. When a plugin with app.run calls actions.play, it is not stated whether a nested overlay step runs with plugins.run semantics (invokable check, target's grants and scope, Via::Service) or under the caller's origin.

The title says gate step 8, but the statement and OP-COM-gate-admit say step 11. The record says fonts.system installs OS-wide, while OP-COM-platform-fonts limits fonts.install to the OS user font folder.
export.render and asset.import accept a path string, but their perms omit PERM-COM-files.paths. OP-FC-export.render lists it, so the common op and the FigCraft op derive permissions differently.

The project.open and project.saveAs 'handle twins' take no handle; both are user-invoked host dialogs. A plugin that already holds a picked handle has to show a second dialog, whereas AE app.open(File) and project.save(File) run silently.

host.installId {scope:'user'} exposes a stable user identity as free and undeclared. Figma requires the 'currentuser' manifest permission for the same data, so this is weaker than the incumbent's enforced permission.

B.claim: Round 2 cut the front off this detail and CON-COM-lifecycle-states. The setup sheet no longer lists permissions, hooks, processes, devices, quota or risk, and the hardware-approve, update-widening-to-Held and quarantine transitions are gone. CAP-COM-setup-widening-sheets was deleted.

The closed list of code kinds is now just 'input-filter, override.' manifest::parse rejects any kind outside the generated set, so effect, panel, tool, brush-engine, audio-effect, format-import, lane and node contributions become undeclarable.

The crash test lost its fault matrix (SIGKILL, SIGSTOP, IPC garbage, arena truncate, device destroy, broker OOM) and its 'app alive' and 'hash equals last commit' checks. Gate, modal, hooks, plugins, GPU, files, input, UI and transaction conformance lost their leading cases too.

All 15 REQ-COM-fc-xdoc rows now have empty details and titles cut mid-sentence. Lost: Run last, Recents and Saved in every app; the parameters.input event; ui.web.open size and position; six new contracts (codegen, widget, text.review and others); EC and PC path ops.

When an ordinary live holder is preempted, its 'flushed prefix commits as its own step' and the rest grafts later. One plugin event then makes two or more undo steps, and a committed partial transaction survives if the remainder later aborts.

PhotoCraft still requires a dialog token and opaque presets to print, but the changed DEC lets a plugin with print pick any local queue and print without a dialog. The DEC also refuses 'network queues', though the OS spooler, not the plugin, does that networking: a restriction with no cause.

The per-plugin bound of 64 owner calls in flight exists only in FigCraft records. The common owner loop and contract leave the queue unbounded, so a flooding plugin can grow owner-queue memory without limit in PhotoCraft and EffectCraft. Meanwhile the common test asserts the cap for every app.

Override is now allowed on view, selection, nudge and tool commands, but the only budget given is 'OwnerFrame'. That is a per-turn owner-drain budget, not a deadline for the guest's reply. No record sets how long an arrow-key nudge or tool command waits before the built-in runs.

On iOS every plugin runs interpreted (wasmi, QuickJS) with no JIT, yet audio.effect (50% of a 1.33 ms block), input.filter (2 ms p99, used by Apple Pencil) and raster.filter CPU budgets apply unchanged, with no iOS rows or degrade rule. Host call overhead is 2 us, but admit alone is 5 us.

This record still says the write-set check applies only to selection scope and that a violation rolls back with -3. CON-SEC-scope-writeset and the bench now apply it to every scope narrower than all and roll back with -2.

The prop 'overridable only on the last seven' reads as if overridable is allowed only on the lifecycle, trust and manager set. The DEC says the opposite: Override is banned there and allowed on view, selection, nudge and tool commands.

The perms list omits files.paths and the root grants (files.known, files.read-home-any, files.write-home-any), and the detail still cites the deleted files.any. OP-COM-export.render also omits files.paths, while OP-FC-export.render lists it.

A.claim: The pixel condition was removed from the sig. canvas.pointer now returns pixel? under PERM-COM-app.events alone, so any event subscriber reads document pixel values under the cursor without document.read.

Gating clauses were cut from intercept hooks. paste lost 'bytes only with clipboard.read', drop lost 'handle only with files.read:picked', command-pattern lost redacted params and re-gating of Rewrite. command-id widened to bare app.intercept.

before-save now returns only 'Edits in one transaction', and before-render returns nothing ('Before: payload'). Both lost findings[] and ask_cancel, but the security records require findings that the host turns into a 'Save anyway' choice.

Sync results over 1 MiB come back as a Handle(Bytes) that is read asynchronously, so UXP synchronous APIs such as fs.readFileSync on a file over 1 MiB cannot return their bytes synchronously as they do in Photoshop.

'1 modal per plugin' blocks nested modal dialogs. That breaks a ScriptUI dialog opening a sub-dialog, nested UXP uxpShowModal or alert inside a dialog, and a PhotoCraft filter editor window opening its own settings dialog.

The test requires that 'a 13th visible page gets 0 -6 Budget results', but the caps table limits each app to 12 visible web renderers and says cap+1 returns -6 Budget. Under CefDocked every T6 panel docks, so a 13th visible UXP or CEP panel fails, which Photoshop and AE never do.

The re-projection budget is 0.5 ms per frame for 100,000 ops, but the caps allow 64 layers × 100,000 ops per plugin, and several plugins can overlay together. At the cap, re-projection is about 30 ms per plugin, which breaks the UI frame guarantee.

Pen regions promise the provisional stroke in the same frame as its sample, but an input filter may take up to a hard 8 ms per batch, almost the whole 8.3 ms frame at 120 Hz. OP-EC-hook.input.filter also states the budget per sample while the contract states it per batch.

Shaping text requires PERM-COM-app.automation, the grant for edits from automatic events. Pure text shaping for a plugin's own UI or canvas is gated with no cause, and font.bytes, which returns the file with its embedding flags, lost its signature.

Three components claim input routing: the contract names CMP-COM-rails, ext-ui-fw says it is 'the one input pump', and CAP-COM-ui-input-events routes via ext-ui-model. The filter-samples prop was cut after 'except', so filtered pen strokes read as automation.

A 4 MiB frame cache cannot hold a HiDPI docked panel: 1000x1200 pt at 2x is about 19 MB of RGBA. WEB1 requires all 10 panels to paint from cache in frame 1. In addition, input is held only 500 ms and then dropped, while a panel takes up to 1.5 s to go live, so clicks are lost.
